severe_bleeding.name: Severe Bleeding Control
steps: Call 911 immediately if bleeding is severe or spurting
Protect yourself - wear gloves if available
Have person lie down and elevate injured area above heart if possible
Apply direct pressure with clean cloth or gauze for 10-15 minutes
If blood soaks through, add more cloth on top - DO NOT remove original
If bleeding continues after 10 minutes of pressure, apply pressure to artery
Once bleeding stops, secure bandage firmly but not too tight
Monitor for shock: pale skin, rapid pulse, weakness
Keep person warm and calm until help arrives
warnings: DO NOT use tourniquet unless trained
DO NOT peek under bandage - keep pressure constant
Call 911 if bleeding won't stop after 15 minutes

choking_adult.name: Choking - Adult (Heimlich Maneuver)
steps: Ask 'Are you choking?' If they can't speak/cough, act immediately
Call 911 or have someone else call
Stand behind person, wrap arms around waist
Make a fist, place thumb side against stomach above navel
Grasp fist with other hand
Give quick, upward thrusts into abdomen
Repeat 5 times, check if object expelled
Continue until object comes out or person becomes unconscious
If unconscious, begin CPR
warnings: DO NOT slap back if person can cough
Call 911 immediately
Even if successful, person should see doctor

cpr_adult.name: CPR - Adult
steps: Call 911 immediately
Check if person is responsive - tap shoulders and shout
Check for breathing - look, listen, feel for 10 seconds
Place person on firm, flat surface
Kneel beside chest
Place heel of one hand on center of chest, other hand on top
Push hard and fast - 2 inches deep, 100-120 compressions per minute
After 30 compressions, give 2 rescue breaths (if trained)
Continue 30:2 ratio until help arrives or person breathes
warnings: DO NOT stop CPR unless person starts breathing
Push HARD - you may break ribs, this is normal
Continue until paramedics arrive

burns_minor.name: Minor Burns (1st/2nd Degree, small area)
steps: Remove person from heat source
Cool burn under cool (not cold) running water for 10-20 minutes
Remove jewelry/tight clothing before swelling starts
DO NOT apply ice - only cool water
Pat dry gently with clean cloth
Apply antibiotic ointment if available
Cover with sterile, non-stick bandage
Take over-the-counter pain reliever if needed
Watch for signs of infection over next few days
warnings: DO NOT pop blisters
DO NOT use butter, oil, or ice
See doctor if burn is larger than 3 inches or on face/hands/genitals

burns_severe.name: Severe Burns (3rd Degree or large area)
steps: Call 911 immediately
Remove person from heat source if safe
DO NOT remove burned clothing stuck to skin
Cover burn with cool, moist, sterile bandage or clean cloth
DO NOT use ice or immerse large burns in water
Elevate burned area above heart if possible
Watch for shock: pale skin, weak pulse, rapid breathing
Keep person warm with blanket (not on burned area)
Stay with person until paramedics arrive
warnings: DO NOT apply ointments or creams
DO NOT break blisters
This is a medical emergency - always call 911

fracture.name: Broken Bone (Fracture)
steps: Call 911 if bone is visible, area is numb, or severe pain
DO NOT move person unless necessary
Immobilize injured area - don't try to realign
Apply ice packs wrapped in cloth (not directly on skin)
Treat for shock if needed: lay person down, elevate legs
If must move person, splint injured area first
For open fracture: cover wound with sterile bandage, don't push bone
Monitor circulation: check if area below injury is pink and warm
warnings: DO NOT try to straighten broken bone
DO NOT move person with suspected spine/neck injury
Always seek medical care for fractures

allergic_reaction.name: Severe Allergic Reaction (Anaphylaxis)
steps: Call 911 immediately if difficulty breathing or swelling
Help person use epinephrine auto-injector (EpiPen) if available
Have person lie down with legs elevated
Loosen tight clothing
DO NOT give anything to drink
Turn person on side if vomiting
Begin CPR if person stops breathing
Stay with person until paramedics arrive
Give paramedics names of any medications/allergens
warnings: This is a life-threatening emergency
Use EpiPen immediately if available
Person needs emergency medical care even after EpiPen
